description.narrative: The objective of Denmark’s support for UNHCR is to address needs in forced displacement contexts and thereby contributing to the achievement of Agenda 2030’s commitment to “leave no one behind” and in particular Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 1, 5, 10 and 161, as well as the main priorities of Denmark’s strategy for development cooperation, The World We Share, relating to poverty, fragility, conflict and creating viable alternatives to forced displacement and irregular migration. It also supports Danish government’s ambition for a fair and humane asylum system within international law by focusing in protection and self-reliance for refugees thus helping refugees in humanitarian settings and areas bordering conflict.

UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, is an UN Agency mandated to provide international protection and assistance to refugees, asylum seekers, refugee returnees, internally displaced persons and stateless persons.
The project in question concerns Danish core funding to the organization in the period 2022-2026 in line with the Organization Strategy for Denmark’s engagement with the UN Office of the High Commissioner for refugees (UNHCR) 2022-2026 which outlines the overall priorities for Denmark’s contributions to and partnership with UNHCR 2022-2026, and is the central platform for Denmark’s dialogue the organization.
Denmark’s priorities for UNHCR's performance in 2022-2026 are set within the overall framework established by UNHCR’s own Strategic Directions and Global Strategic Priorities. UNHCR’s Strategic Directions for 2017-2021 elaborate five core directions on which UNHCR will focus – protection, responding in emergencies and beyond, promoting inclusion and self-reliance, including through the engagement of development actors, the empowerment of the people UNHCR serves, and the pursuit of solutions.
Within the broader objective of protecting conflict affected populations, it is a particular priority for Denmark to address complex challenges related to forced displacement and irregular migration, to strengthen protection of refugees and IDP’s, and to find durable solutions for refugees and IDP’s, including ensuring rights of women and girls. Further a strengthened focus on climate and environmental sustainability as well as development of deeper partnerships with implementing partners as well as development partners in and beyond the UN system in line with the objectives of the GCR is of priority to Denmark.
